note: Everything to build, in the order it will be done. Set by Jesse on 13 Nov 2026: the agent work first, then the paper, then zero-knowledge and joint computation, then the thesis, then wider testing and adoption. Careful thinking is done by Fable; plumbing by Opus.

phases.title: The reference agent and this explorer
phases.goal: A real agent built to the reference design, a site that replays what it did, and a narrated walkthrough.

items.title: Reference design
items.detail: Two gates around a black-box core, five inbound and six outbound checks, four stores, the verifiable message.

items.title: Check against OWASP, W3C and current practice
items.detail: Terms aligned; ten added requirements; see the Requirements view.

items.title: Explorer site
items.detail: Step-through and play modes, a selector per layer, message inspector, guided tour.

items.title: Reference agent package
items.detail: Lifted from the September pilot: named gates, a suite registry, a trace for every decision.

items.title: Real traces: main flow and three failures
items.detail: Mortgage in principle; over-ask refused; offer outside limits; injected instruction stopped.

items.title: Swap the transport
items.detail: The same flow over email, MCP and A2A, with the same verdicts.

items.title: Product index and sector register
items.detail: Find lenders through a trusted index with no personal data; check them on a register.

items.title: Step-up challenge
items.detail: A bank asks for a certified face check before it accepts the mandate.

items.title: Joint computation as a data-sharing option
items.detail: Two banks and the agent work out a total; the lender sees only the total.

items.title: Data by reference on Solid
items.detail: Grant read access in the pod and send a pointer with terms, instead of a copy.

items.title: When things go wrong
items.detail: Accountability flows you can switch between: a claim to a regulator, fault passed to the vendor, reputation.

items.title: Narrated walkthrough video
items.detail: Slides, then the site, with pointing and captions.

items.title: Comparison with the agents already built
items.detail: The pilot, the suite agent and the policy sandbox drawn against the reference design, with gaps.

items.title: A core that is a real model
items.detail: Recorded runs with a model as the core, after the weekly usage reset on 17 Nov.

phases.title: The specification family
phases.goal: One core document and a document per layer, written so someone else could implement them.

items.title: Core specification
items.detail: Roles, the verifiable message, the checks and their outcomes, the record, configurations.

items.title: Ten layer specifications
items.detail: For each layer: what a suite must define, and the suites registered so far.

items.title: Baseline configuration
items.detail: The recommended default, one suite per layer, so two strangers' agents can always talk.

items.title: Conformance
items.detail: The trace format, expected outlines, and the rule: no suite without a trace.

items.title: Mortgage profile
items.detail: The claims, accepted sources and assurance levels for the worked example.

items.title: Vocabulary
items.detail: Terms and reason codes as an ontology, governed on Concord.

items.title: Zero-knowledge query proof suite
items.detail: Bring the existing zero-knowledge specifications in as an authenticity suite.

phases.title: The paper
phases.goal: Bring what the implementation taught us back into the paper.

items.title: Review the paper against the implementation
items.detail: Where the seven gaps held up, where the design changed, what is missing.

items.title: Propose a new version
items.detail: A set of changes, laid as suggestions in the paper's document.

phases.title: Zero-knowledge and joint computation
phases.goal: Review and update the specifications, papers and code.

items.title: Review the zero-knowledge specifications and architecture
items.detail: Against the authenticity layer and the query-proof suite.

items.title: Review the joint computation specification and paper
items.detail: Against the data-sharing suite built in P1.9.

items.title: Updated specifications, papers and implementations
items.detail: Proposed as changes on the engine's own project.

phases.title: Thesis first draft
phases.goal: A first full pass, including a study of how trust is governed today.

items.title: Landscape study of governance
items.detail: eIDAS, the UK digital identity and attributes trust framework, GLEIF and vLEI, sector registers, legal accountability, agent registries.

items.title: Which frameworks to build on
items.detail: What can be used as it is, what is missing, and the shortest path to working infrastructure.

items.title: Full first draft
items.detail: All chapters, drawing on the paper, the specifications and the implementation.

phases.title: Real use cases
phases.goal: Show the same design works between people, between a person and a business, between businesses, and inside one.

items.title: Catalog of use cases by context
items.detail: Person to person, business to consumer, business to business to consumer, business to business, internal agents.

items.title: A scenario and traces for each
items.detail: Each use case run as a scenario in this explorer.

items.title: Review of where the design fits and where it does not
items.detail: Written up per context.

phases.title: Adoption
phases.goal: A name, a default, and a way for someone to start with nothing but email.

items.title: A name
items.detail: Options with a recommendation, for Jesse to choose.

items.title: Email footer upgrade path
items.detail: "I use an agent that supports this" with a link; plain email still works, and both sides upgrade when they can.

items.title: Setup page
items.detail: How to get an agent: connect an existing assistant through an adapter, or sign up to a hosted one.

items.title: Bring the suite's own agent up to the reference design
items.detail: Its channels do not yet verify signatures and it has no memory at runtime.
